children: Bharti Airtel Limited (NSE:BHARTIARTL) is hiking postpaid tariffs and boosting ARPU while expanding offerings—from Starlink distribution and Fast Lane 5G slicing to sovereign cloud, data centers and enterprise security—awaiting regulatory clearances that could unlock further revenue and rerating.
Previous Week Recap
Bharti Airtel Tariffs Risen
: Bharti Airtel raised postpaid tariffs by ₹50 from Oct 8, 2026 (e.g., ₹449→₹499); subscribers moved to nearest higher plan; plans add one annual 5-day roaming pack; stock rose ~2.4% intraday
ARPU 264, 30M Postpaid
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) reported ARPU of ₹264 and 30M postpaid subscribers (June 30). Quarterly postpaid adds ~1.0–1.1M; company expects long‑term ARPU to exceed ₹300 as postpaid share rises.
Starlink In India Partner

: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) signed a March 2025 deal to distribute SpaceX Starlink satellite broadband in India, pending SpaceX approvals; Airtel is named as a Starlink partner for Indian operations.
Motilal Oswal Buy Rating
: Motilal Oswal kept a Buy on Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) with a ₹2,250 target, citing attractive risk-reward and potential re-rating from Jio Platforms' proposed IPO.
Jio IPO Could Lift Tariffs
: Prospects of Reliance Jio listing and market scrutiny could push sector tariffs up 12–15% by Dec 2026, potentially lifting Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) ARPU and margins if realized
Data Center Expansion 1GW
: Bharti Airtel plans to expand data center capacity to 1 GW. CEO Shashwat Sharma says the unit has anchor demand, strong returns, and is a long‑term, 20–25 year profit opportunity.
Security Clearances Delays Launch
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) awaits Home Ministry security clearance and final DoT/TRAI pricing and revenue-sharing rules for satellite services, delaying the operator’s commercial launch plans.
Fast Lane 5G Slicing
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) rolled out Fast Lane using 5G slicing to boost network quality and is pushing bundle upgrade plans combining data, family lines, entertainment and international roaming.
Sovereign Cloud For Regulated Workloads

: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) launched a sovereign cloud to keep sensitive Indian data local, targeting healthcare, energy, banking and identity clients to host regulated workloads and meet data rules.
Railways SOC, 6G Prep
: Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) runs a security operations center for Indian Railways and is upgrading network infrastructure to support future 6G rollout, building on its 4G/5G deployments.
This is an AI-generated summary and may contain inaccuracies. Please verify any important information with the original sources.

title: Weekly Recap: ₹50 postpaid hike, stock +2.4% and ARPU ₹264, 30M postpaid
